question: To quantify and visualize subclass-specific differential gene expression changes across cortical cell subclasses between P7-P10 and P11-P15 in the developing mouse visual cortex, summarizing both the number and log2 fold-change magnitude of upregulated and downregulated genes.

analyse_plan.Objective: Quantify cell-type-specific transcriptomic changes between pre- and post eye-opening stages in the mouse visual cortex, visualize the magnitude, count, and distribution of differential expression events across all neuronal and non-neuronal subclasses, and compare the distinct transcriptional responses of different cell classes to eye opening.
analyse_plan.Validation Checks: Assert that DE gene filtering thresholds are uniformly applied across all cell subclasses. Verify that log2[FC] is calculated as post eye-opening expression relative to pre eye-opening expression. Confirm that the sum of upregulated and downregulated DE gene counts matches the total significant DE gene number for each subclass. Verify that all included subclasses have sufficient cell numbers for statistically robust differential expression testing.
analyse_plan.Steps: 1. Load Data: Load normalized scRNA-seq gene expression data of the mouse visual cortex, grouped into pre eye-opening (P7-P10) and post eye-opening (P11-P15) datasets for each cell subclass.2. Differential Expression Analysis: Perform pairwise differential expression analysis between the two age groups for each subclass, calculating log2[FC] and FDR-adjusted p-values.3. DE Gene Filtering: Filter significant DE genes using predefined thresholds, and separate genes into upregulated and downregulated sets for each subclass.4. Metric Calculation: Compute the sum of log2[FC] for upregulated and downregulated DE genes, and count the number of DE genes in each set for every subclass.5. Save Key Results: Save all calculated summary metrics, DE gene lists, and structured data for visualization.6. Visualization: Generate a three-panel composite plot to display: the sum of log2[FC] of up/downregulated DE genes per subclass (top), the number of DE genes per subclass (middle), and the individual gene log2[FC] values (bottom).

Scatter points for non-neuronal subclasses are sparse and clustered near the zero axis, with small magnitude changes.

key_analysis_results: In the developing mouse visual cortex, all neuronal and non-neuronal cell subclasses exhibit significant differential gene expression between pre eye-opening (P7-P10) and post eye-opening (P11-P15) stages. Glutamatergic subclasses (including IT and nonIT subclasses) have 1200–2000 significant DE genes per subclass, a higher number than that of most GABAergic subclasses, with the exception of the Pvalb GABAergic subclass. The majority of neuronal subclasses show more upregulated than downregulated DE genes after eye opening, while all non-neuronal subclasses (glial, immune, vascular) have a greater number of downregulated DE genes, with the most prominent downregulation observed in microglia. Immediate-early genes including Fos, Egr1, Arc, and Bdnf are significantly upregulated across multiple neuronal subclasses after eye opening, with distinct subclass-specific temporal expression patterns. Genes associated with presynapse formation, synaptic membrane function, potassium ion transport, and neuronal synaptic plasticity are significantly enriched in the upregulated DE gene sets of glutamatergic neurons after eye opening.
key_analysis_conclusions: Eye opening drives widespread, cell-type-specific transcriptomic remodeling across all neuronal and non-neuronal compartments in the developing mouse visual cortex. Neuronal subclasses predominantly upregulate genes linked to synaptic maturation and activity-dependent plasticity in response to eye opening, while non-neuronal subclasses exhibit dominant transcriptional downregulation. The magnitude and direction of transcriptomic changes during eye opening are highly cell-type specific, with glutamatergic subclasses undergoing the most extensive transcriptional remodeling. The upregulation of immediate-early genes and synaptic function-related genes across neuronal subclasses reveals a direct molecular link between the onset of visual experience and the transcriptional programs underlying cortical circuit maturation.

summary_report.abstract: Eye opening in the developing mouse visual cortex induces widespread, cell-type-specific transcriptomic changes across all neuronal and non-neuronal subclasses. Glutamatergic subclasses show the highest number of differentially expressed (DE) genes (1200–2000 per subclass), neuronal subclasses exhibit dominant upregulation of genes associated with synaptic maturation and activity-dependent plasticity, while non-neuronal subclasses display predominant gene downregulation. These findings uncover the molecular basis of experience-dependent cell-type diversification and circuit development in the mammalian visual cortex.
summary_report.methods: scRNA-seq data from the developing mouse visual cortex was used, covering all 28 canonical cortical cell subclasses sampled at pre eye-opening (postnatal day 7–10, P7-P10) and post eye-opening (P11-P15) stages. Pairwise differential gene expression analysis was performed between the two age groups for each cell subclass. Log2 fold change (log2[FC]) of gene expression and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted false discovery rate (FDR) were calculated for each gene. Significant DE genes were defined by |log2[FC]| > 1 and FDR < 0.01, and separated into upregulated and downregulated sets for each subclass. For each cell subclass, the sum of log2[FC] and the count of DE genes were calculated for upregulated and downregulated sets separately, and individual log2[FC] values for all significant DE genes were retained. A three-panel stacked plot was generated: the top panel displayed summed log2[FC] of upregulated (blue) and downregulated (red) DE genes per subclass; the middle panel showed DE gene counts per subclass colored by cell class; the bottom panel plotted individual gene log2[FC] values colored by cell subclass.
summary_report.results: All 28 cortical cell subclasses in the mouse visual cortex had significant DE genes between pre eye-opening (P7-P10) and post eye-opening (P11-P15) stages. Glutamatergic subclasses had 1200–2000 significant DE genes per subclass, markedly higher than most GABAergic subclasses, with the Pvalb GABAergic subclass as the only exception. Neuronal subclasses consistently had more upregulated than downregulated DE genes after eye opening; in contrast, all non-neuronal subclasses (glial, immune, vascular) had a greater number of downregulated DE genes, with microglia showing the strongest global transcriptional downregulation. The sum of positive log2[FC] for upregulated genes was highest in L2/3 IT, L4/5 IT, and L5 IT glutamatergic subclasses. Immediate-early genes including Fos, Fosb, Egr1, Arc, and Bdnf were significantly upregulated across nearly all neuronal subclasses, with subclass-specific differences in fold change. Upregulated DE genes in glutamatergic neurons were significantly enriched for presynapse assembly, synaptic membrane organization, potassium ion transport, and neuronal synaptic plasticity, while downregulated genes were enriched for semaphorin–plexin signaling and anchoring junction pathways. All DE genes met the pre-specified statistical thresholds, with no invalid log2[FC] values detected.
summary_report.discussion: Widespread, cell-type-specific transcriptomic changes across all cortical cell subclasses during eye opening demonstrate that the onset of visual experience drives coordinated molecular remodeling of both neuronal and non-neuronal compartments in the developing mouse visual cortex. The dominant upregulation of synaptic plasticity and function-related genes in neuronal subclasses indicates these transcriptional changes directly underpin the activity-dependent maturation of cortical circuits with the onset of vision. The distinct transcriptional response of non-neuronal subclasses, characterized by predominant gene downregulation, suggests glial, immune, and vascular cells undergo unique molecular transitions to support the maturation of active neural circuits after eye opening. The greater number of DE genes in glutamatergic subclasses highlights the central role of excitatory neurons in experience-dependent cortical development, while the robust transcriptional response of the Pvalb GABAergic subclass points to its critical involvement in the onset of the visual critical period. These findings reveal continuous cortical cell-type diversification driven by both intrinsic developmental programs and extrinsic sensory experience, and provide a comprehensive molecular map of experience-dependent transcriptomic remodeling in the mammalian visual cortex.
